title: Eco-Safe Driving
whatItIs: Driving with economy and the environment in mind: plan ahead, keep moving smoothly and use the highest suitable gear, without ever reducing safety.
keyFacts: Never reduce safety to improve economy.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT leave an engine running unnecessarily while stationary on a public road.

keyFacts: Stopped for more than a couple of minutes? Apply the parking brake and switch off (you may leave it running in traffic).
Fuel use goes up with extra load, wrongly inflated tyres and wind resistance, e.g. a loaded roof rack.
On the test, eco-safe driving is assessed over the whole drive but doesn't affect the result.

items.title: Plan ahead
items.text: Look well ahead for lights, signs and hazards, and adjust speed smoothly.

items.title: Highest responsive gear
items.text: Use the highest gear that won't labour the engine. Avoid high revs.

items.title: Slow down early
items.text: Foresee stops and decelerate smoothly: less fuel used, less wear.

items.title: Cut weight and drag
items.text: Remove load you don't need. Keep tyres at the right pressure.

a.label: Fuel-efficient
points: Keep moving when it's safe to
Scan ahead and adjust speed smoothly

onTheTest.question: A candidate has a fault marked in the 'Eco-safe driving' boxes. How does it affect the test result?
options: It doesn't, but the examiner will debrief it
It counts as one driving fault
It counts as a serious fault
It's only recorded on a fail
onTheTest.why: DT1 1.33: fuel-efficient driving does not contribute to the test result. If an eco-safe fault is recorded, pass or fail, the examiner debriefs the candidate.

onTheTest.question: A pupil asks if rolling downhill in neutral saves fuel safely. What's the best reply?
options: No: coasting reduces your control of the car
Yes, if the clutch is held down
onTheTest.why: Rule 122: coasting removes engine braking, lets speed build quickly downhill and can affect steering and gear selection.

traps: Choosing safety over an eco technique is correct: the examiner takes that into account.
Changing down when road speed is too high wastes fuel with no gain in safety.
Eco-safe driving has two headings on the report: control and planning.
